18:00 Local Time, 12:30 GMT: The two umpires have a chat and they've decided that light isn't good enough for play to continue. So, it's stumps on day one. As expected, India have dominated proceedings after winning a crucial toss. The Sri Lankan pacers weren't disciplined with the new ball and that allowed the Indian openers to get their eye in. Yashasvi Jaiswal fell against the run of play, he was unfortunately run-out for 32 after the bowler collided with him. That was the only wicket in the opening session where the visitors scored 101 runs.

Rain delayed the start of the second session, but once it began, the two Karnataka batters batted with ease. Both Padikkal and Rahul notched up their respective fifties and Sri Lanka failed to create any chances in the middle session. Rahul was unable to bat after the Tea break due to cramps and that brought Gill out to the middle. While he saw DDP register his maiden Test ton, a classy innings, the Indian skipper holed out while trying to be aggressive against Prabath. Following another brief period of showers, there was an interesting duel between Pant and the spinners. Some solid blocks, a few plays and misses and unsurprisingly four aggressive boundaries. There's enough in the pitch for the spinners to trouble the batters but it's fair to say that SL weren't consistent. Will they make amends? Or will India continue to consolidate their position? Tune in tomorrow (early start at 09.45 AM) to find out how the action unfolds.

09:10 Local Time, 03:40 GMT, 09:10 IST: Day 2: The opening day belonged to India, Devdutt Padikkal in particular. The left-handed batter got off the mark first ball with an authoritative boundary, batted at a good tempo throughout the day to record his first Test century and put his team in a strong position. On a rain-marred day, Sri Lanka bowled 73 overs but couldn't exert pressure for long periods of time. Although there weren't any dry patches on the pitch, there was sharp turn for the spinners every now and then.

Occasional showers, good batting conditions for the first few days and then spinners to rule the roost. That's how things usually unfold in Galle and hence it's a result-oriented venue. Let's see how this Test pans out. The second new ball will be due in 7 overs. And as long Pant is out in the middle, runs will come quickly. The hosts can't afford to have another bad day.

Padikkal (2/2): [On what makes this hundred special] Patience for me, I think it was more to do with what I have gone through before this game. I think my last Test was in 2024, so it's been a long time coming, and I've had to patiently wait, look on from the outside. It's never easy, but at the same time it gave me time to really work on my game, to perfect things in my game that I felt needed perfecting. And I'm really glad that all that hard work came to effect today. Was a bit nervous towards the end when I got closer to it, but I think that's part of it, and really happy to get over the line. [On playing at Galle] Especially this ground, I think even when we came here with the India A side, I got a few runs, and even in the warm-up game obviously I got some runs.
